note: The signed bytes are the label, purpose, decision, target, approver, request digest, nonce, authority generation and expiry, in that order, each behind a 4-byte big-endian length. Text is UTF-8, the digest is 32 raw bytes, generation and expiry (ms since 1970) are 8-byte big-endian. Signatures are P-256 ECDSA SHA-256, IEEE P1363 r||s, base64. In every case the signature is a real one over signed.fields by signed.key; the verifier gets record, answer, now, used_nonces and the state (a case's state fields replace the top-level ones) and must answer expect, with reason when refused. It rebuilds the bytes from its record and never reads signed. Where signed.damaged is set, the answer's signature is the real one (signed.signature_p1363) damaged as described. state.generation is the device's current authority generation: the verifier does not read it, the signed generation is the record's. bad_keys are public keys a verifier must itself reject (off the curve, the point at infinity, another curve) and r or s outside 1..n-1 must be rejected the same way, not left to the crypto provider.

cross_purpose.note: One approval signature per purpose over the same record. Presented for a record of the same purpose it is approved; for every other purpose it is refused with bad_signature (the answer states the record's purpose).
